item.title: Blue Wahoos' Historic Season Ends With Playoff Loss to Shuckers
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos saw one of their best seasons come to an end Tuesday night, falling 8-3 to the Biloxi Shuckers in playoff action. The loss eliminated the Double-A affiliate of the Minnesota Twins from postseason contention, cutting short what had been a remarkably successful campaign at Admiral Fetterman Stadium. The Blue Wahoos had…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos saw one of their best seasons come to an end Tuesday night, falling 8-3 to the Biloxi Shuckers in playoff action. The loss eliminated the Double-A affiliate of the Minnesota Twins from postseason contention, cutting short what had been a remarkably successful campaign at Admiral Fetterman Stadium.

The Blue Wahoos had built one of the most competitive rosters in franchise history this season, but couldn't overcome the Shuckers' offense in the elimination game. Biloxi's eight runs proved too much for Pensacola's bats to overcome in the decisive matchup.

The playoff exit marks the end of what the team and local fans will remember as a special year, despite the heartbreaking finish. The Blue Wahoos will look to build on this foundation when spring training returns next season.

item.content:encoded:
Firefighters from multiple agencies responded Thursday afternoon to a significant fire deep in a wooded area west of Walnut Hill, battling both a logging equipment blaze and the resulting brush fire that spread through the forest.

The fire broke out off Highway 97A in a remote section of North Escambia County, requiring crews to navigate dense woods to reach the equipment fire. The initial equipment blaze then ignited surrounding brush and timber, creating a more complex firefighting operation.

Details on the exact cause of the logging equipment fire, the acreage burned, and which agencies responded were not immediately available. The remote location in the wooded area presented additional challenges for firefighting operations.

item.title: Warm, Sunny Weekend Ahead for NW Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents can expect pleasant weather through the weekend, with sunshine dominating and temperatures climbing into the low 90s. Friday will bring sunny skies with a high near 91 degrees and minimal wind from the northeast around 5 mph, according to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia. Conditions remain clear…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents can expect pleasant weather through the weekend, with sunshine dominating and temperatures climbing into the low 90s.

Friday will bring sunny skies with a high near 91 degrees and minimal wind from the northeast around 5 mph, according to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia. Conditions remain clear overnight, with lows dropping to around 70 degrees and calm winds making for comfortable sleeping temperatures.

Saturday shapes up similarly warm with highs reaching near 94 degrees. A slight 20 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms develops after 1 p.m., but most of the day should remain dry and sunny. Winds will be light, shifting from the north around 5 mph before calming completely through the afternoon.

item.title: Free Health Screenings, Food Drive Coming to Century Senior Event Today

item.content:encoded:
The Council on Aging of West Florida is hosting a resource fair today aimed at connecting older adults in northern Escambia County with expanded services and community support.

The event in Century will offer free health screenings, food assistance, and supplies for residents age 60 and older. According to the Council on Aging, the gathering is designed to make it easier for seniors in the area to learn about and enroll in available programs without having to travel to other parts of the county.

Organizers say the event brings together various community resources under one roof, allowing older adults to address multiple needs in a single visit. The screening component may help identify health concerns that could benefit from early intervention or ongoing care coordination.

Seniors interested in attending should contact the Council on Aging of West Florida for specific event timing and location details in Century.

item.title: Pensacola Postal Worker Admits Stealing Marijuana From Mail
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Vincent M., employed at the facility, admitted to removing cannabis from parcels that were being sorted and processed. The theft was discovered during a federal…
item.content:encoded:
A 25-year-old postal worker has pleaded guilty in federal court to stealing marijuana from packages passing through the mail processing facility in Pensacola, according to court records.

Vincent M., employed at the facility, admitted to removing cannabis from parcels that were being sorted and processed. The theft was discovered during a federal investigation into mail tampering at the processing center.

The case was handled in U.S. District Court, where the postal worker entered his guilty plea. Sentencing details and the specific quantity of marijuana involved were not immediately disclosed.

The U.S. Postal Service has not commented publicly on security measures being reviewed at the Pensacola facility following the discovery.

Registration forms and releases are available online, and the school is encouraging community members, local businesses, and student organizations to take part in the annual celebration.

item.content:encoded: The J.M. Tate High School AJROTC Aggie Battalion held its annual remembrance march on September 11, bringing together cadets to honor those lost in the 2001 terrorist attacks. The solemn ceremony is part of the school's tradition of marking the date each year, keeping the memory of the nearly 3,000 lives lost alive for a new generation of North Escambia students. AJROTC programs across the nation use September 11 as a teaching moment about service, sacrifice, and citizenship. Tate's observance reflects the military values instilled in the cadets through the Junior ROTC curriculum, which prepares high school students for potential military service and leadership roles.

item.title: Century OKs $8.48M Budget With Steady Property Tax Rate
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Century Town Council has tentatively approved an $8.48 million budget for the coming fiscal year, maintaining its property tax millage rate at 1.0405 mills, according to reporting from North Escambia. The council's action Thursday night keeps the town's property tax burden flat, meaning homeowners in the Century area will not see an increase…
item.content:encoded:
The Century Town Council has tentatively approved an $8.48 million budget for the coming fiscal year, maintaining its property tax millage rate at 1.0405 mills, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The council's action Thursday night keeps the town's property tax burden flat, meaning homeowners in the Century area will not see an increase in their ad valorem tax bills tied to the millage rate itself.

The budget approval comes as Century, like many local governments across Santa Rosa County, navigates ongoing expenses for municipal services, infrastructure, and operations. The tentative vote allows the town to move forward with planning while final adoption is expected at a later council meeting.

While some businesses like Indigo Denim Bar and Boutique have avoided water intrusion so far, owner Katie Bosso expressed concern about the flooding risk,…
item.content:encoded:
Recent heavy rain in downtown Pensacola has raised alarms among business owners along Palafox Street after nearly two inches of rain fell in just 30 minutes, according to WKRG News 5.

While some businesses like Indigo Denim Bar and Boutique have avoided water intrusion so far, owner Katie Bosso expressed concern about the flooding risk, particularly for nearby shops that were affected during the deluge.

The incident highlights ongoing drainage and flooding challenges in downtown Pensacola's main commercial corridor. Business owners are now weighing the vulnerability of their operations to heavy rain events and considering what infrastructure improvements might be needed to protect their storefronts and merchandise.

The flooding raises questions about stormwater management in the historic district as the area continues to see development and investment.

According to WKRG News 5, Robertsdale High School head coach Justin Jones filed suit against the Alabama High School Athletic Association, the Baldwin County Board of Education, and school…
item.content:encoded:
A high school football coach in nearby Baldwin County is taking legal action against state athletic officials following what he says was an unjust suspension. According to WKRG News 5, Robertsdale High School head coach Justin Jones filed suit against the Alabama High School Athletic Association, the Baldwin County Board of Education, and school principal William White after Jones and ten players were suspended from competition.

The lawsuit centers on the circumstances surrounding the suspensions, though specific details about what led to the disciplinary action were not immediately disclosed. Jones' legal challenge names both state and local education authorities, suggesting he disputes the decision at multiple levels of the athletic hierarchy.

The case comes as high school athletics continue to draw scrutiny over how governing bodies handle player and coach discipline. The AHSAA, which oversees athletic programs across Alabama, has broad authority to enforce rules governing student-athletes and school personnel.

item.content:encoded:

Residents needing library services during the closure can visit other Escambia County library branches. More details about the scope of repairs and a precise reopening timeline are expected from county officials.

item.content:encoded:
A teacher at Fairhope West Elementary is receiving an outpouring of support from her community after being diagnosed with a rare and aggressive form of brain cancer, according to WKRG News 5.

What began as one family facing an extraordinarily difficult medical situation has blossomed into a broader community response, with neighbors, fellow educators, and local residents stepping up to help during the challenging treatment process ahead.

The diagnosis represents the kind of personal health crisis that often brings communities together, particularly in smaller Alabama towns where school staff are woven into the fabric of local life. The teacher's colleagues and students' families have begun organizing support efforts to help ease the burden on her and her family during this time.

The rare nature of her cancer diagnosis underscores how such illnesses can strike unexpectedly, even among people in their productive years who are actively serving their communities in education.

item.title: Escambia, Santa Rosa shellfish areas reopen after water quality review

The reopening comes after the department completed a water quality review of the affected areas. Shellfish harvesting…
item.content:encoded:
Florida health officials have given the all-clear for shellfish harvesting to resume in portions of Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties, according to an announcement from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services.

The reopening comes after the department completed a water quality review of the affected areas. Shellfish harvesting had been restricted in these zones while state officials evaluated conditions to ensure the waters met safety standards for commercial and recreational harvesting.

Local oyster and clam harvesters can now return to these areas. The department's decision reflects improved water quality conditions in the region, though residents should continue to monitor for any future closure notices.

item.title: FPL Completes 2,000 Miles of Underground Power Lines Statewide
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Power & Light has reached a significant infrastructure milestone, completing the conversion of 2,000 miles of overhead power lines to underground across Florida, according to WKRG News 5. The utility's underground conversion program represents an ongoing effort to improve reliability and reduce service disruptions caused by severe weather.…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Power & Light has reached a significant infrastructure milestone, completing the conversion of 2,000 miles of overhead power lines to underground across Florida, according to WKRG News 5.

The utility's underground conversion program represents an ongoing effort to improve reliability and reduce service disruptions caused by severe weather. Underground lines are less vulnerable to damage from high winds, lightning, and falling tree limbs—a major concern in Florida during hurricane season.

Escambia County residents have benefited from portions of this statewide initiative. The conversions typically target residential neighborhoods, with the underground infrastructure reducing outage frequency and restoration times during major storms.

FPL has not announced a specific timeline for completing additional conversions, but the company says the 2,000-mile achievement reflects its commitment to modernizing the state's electrical grid.

item.title: Patronis votes to block AI data center costs from shifting to Florida households
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's District 1 representative Jimmy Patronis has backed legislation aimed at preventing American households from footing the bill for expanding artificial intelligence data centers across the country. According to a news release, Patronis voted to advance the measure, which would shield residents from bearing infrastructure costs typically…
item.content:encoded: Florida's District 1 representative Jimmy Patronis has backed legislation aimed at preventing American households from footing the bill for expanding artificial intelligence data centers across the country. According to a news release, Patronis voted to advance the measure, which would shield residents from bearing infrastructure costs typically associated with large-scale AI facilities. The bill represents an effort by lawmakers to address concerns that deployment expenses for data centers—critical infrastructure supporting AI development—could eventually be passed along to consumers through utility costs or other means. Patronis, whose district includes Escambia County, characterized the vote as a step toward protecting local residents from unexpected financial burdens as the AI industry expands. The legislation still requires additional congressional action before becoming law.
